events.title: C++11 standard published (ISO/IEC 14882:2011)
events.summary: ISO/IEC 14882:2011 was published on September 1, 2011 — the C++11 standard with auto, lambdas, move semantics, and smart pointers.
events.about: C++11 modernized the language after a 13-year gap: `auto`, range-for, `std::thread`, `unique_ptr`/`shared_ptr`, lambdas, and rvalue references. Code that once needed Boost can now use the standard library. Most new C++ today is written in C++11 dialect or later.

narrative.whyChosen: C++11 is the biggest leap in C++ since templates — it changed how everyday C++ is written.
narrative.whyImportant: Move semantics and smart pointers fixed memory-management patterns; lambdas and auto reduced boilerplate across the ecosystem.
narrative.problemSolved: C++98/03 felt dated next to Java and C#; developers needed modern abstractions without giving up performance.
